item.title: Local Optimality of the d-cube for Laplacian Eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2610.30463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each $d \ge 2$ we prove that the unit $d$-cube $\square_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is, on the class $\mathcal{P}$ of convex polytopes combinatorially equivalent to a $d$-cube, (i) a strict local minimizer of the scale-invariant isoperimetric ratio $I(\Omega) = \tfrac{P(\Omega)^d}{|\Omega|^{d-1}}$, with $P$ the perimeter, (ii) a strict local minimizer of the volume-normalized first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\bar\lambda(\Omega) = |\Omega|^{2/d}\lambda_1(\Omega)$, and (iii) a strict local maximizer of the volume-normalized first Neumann eigenvalue $\bar\mu(\Omega) = |\Omega|^{2/d}\mu_1(\Omega)$. The method is a shape-derivative Hessian analysis adapted to the hyperoctahedral symmetry of the cube. In symmetry-adapted coordinates on the parameter space --- the decomposition into irreducible representations of the hyperoctahedral group --- each Hessian is block-diagonal, with four scalar eigenvalues, which we give in closed form in $\pi$, rational coefficients, and a few universal series-constants. The first Neumann eigenvalue is not differentiable at $\square_d$, since its lowest cluster splits under perturbation. The Neumann case therefore works with a smooth auxiliary functional, whose Hessian is computed by second-order perturbation theory of the cluster; the coupling to modes outside the cluster enters at the same order. Finally, we show that extremality of $I$, $\bar\lambda$, and $\bar\mu$ does not hold in high dimensions for a particular multilinear perturbation that leaves $\mathcal{P}$ by breaking convexity. All results are local; we discuss why a global statement, available for quadrilaterals (Endo and Osting, 2026), appears out of reach for $d \ge 3$.
item.dc:creator: Braxton Osting, Robert Viator

item.title: Optimal Hardy weights for the fractional discrete Dirichlet Laplacian on the half-line
item.description:
arXiv:2610.31171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For positive powers of the discrete Dirichlet Laplacian $(-\Delta_{\mathrm{D}})^{\sigma}$, non-trivial Hardy weights exist if and only if $0<\sigma<3/2$. For $0<\sigma\leq 1$, an explicit optimal Hardy weight for $(-\Delta_{\mathrm{D}})^\sigma$ was obtained by Das and de la Fuente-Fern'{a}ndez. Their ground state argument does not apply when $1<\sigma<3/2$, because the off-diagonal matrix entries of $(-\Delta_{\mathrm{D}})^\sigma$ are no longer all non-positive. Nevertheless, we show that their result is true for the entire subcriticality range $0<\sigma<3/2$. For $1<\sigma<3/2$, our argument combines the factorisation $$(-\Delta_{\mathrm{D}})^{\sigma}=
abla_{\mathrm{D}}^{*}(-\Delta_{\mathrm{N}})^{\sigma-1}
abla_{\mathrm{D}},$$ where $
abla_{\mathrm{D}}$ and $-\Delta_{\mathrm{N}}$ are the discrete Dirichlet gradient and the discrete Neumann Laplacian, respectively, with a suitable two-term ground state representation. In addition, we use these arguments to derive another explicit family of optimal Hardy weights for any $\sigma\in(0,3/2)$.
item.dc:creator: Franti\v{s}ek \v{S}tampach, Jakub Waclawek

item.title: Lower bounds on Steklov eigenfunctions for a class of curvilinear polygons
item.description: arXiv:2610.31387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Steklov eigenfunctions, $\{\phi_{\sigma_j}\}_{j=0}^\infty$, are the eigenfunctions of the Dirichlet to Neumann map on a bounded domain with eigenvalue $\sigma_j$. This paper considers Steklov eigenfunctions and eigenvalues on a family of curvilinear polygons, $\Omega_\alpha$ whose boundaries are smooth away from a single corner of angle $\alpha$. We (i) prove optimal lower bounds on the decay of the harmonic extension, $u_{\sigma_j}$, of $\phi_{\sigma_j}$ away from the boundary of $\Omega_\alpha$ and (ii) give optimal lower bounds on the degree to which the high energy Steklov spectrum of $\Omega_\alpha\setminus H_1$ may differ from that of $\Omega_\alpha\setminus H_0$ when $H_1$ and $H_0$ are isometric. This shows that the corresponding estimates in recent work by the authors together with Malagutti are optimal. The proof in this paper was obtained through an interaction with ChatGPT 6 Astra: While writing the work with Malagutti, the authors became curious about optimal error bounds for the difference between the Steklov spectra on a curvilinear polygon, $P$, and the spectrum of any operator which knows only local information about $\partial P$. The authors suggested to ChatGPT to remove two isometric, smooth domains from a curvilinear polygon. ChatGPT suggested the ideas for a proof based on a regularized trace and the singularity in the kernel of the DtN map near a corner. The authors then suggested a simpler, conformal approach, the method for handling small angles, and the idea to obtain lower bounds on Steklov eigenfunctions. The paper is entirely written by the authors and the argument has been significantly modified, clarified, and simplified from the ChatGPT ideas.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Galkowski, Ruoyu P. T. Wang

item.title: P\'olya's conjecture for Neumann eigenvalues of spherical shells
item.description: arXiv:2610.31464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the strict P\'olya inequality for Neumann eigenvalues of spherical shells in every dimension $d\ge2$, for every radius ratio and every positive energy. The proof also covers balls. For shells, the excess over the leading Weyl term has a positive lower bound depending only on dimension. Above explicit frequency thresholds independent of the radius ratio, we obtain a surplus of boundary order. These estimates remain uniform as the hole shrinks or the shell becomes thin. We compare weighted sampling errors for inverse radial actions while retaining the removed volume exactly. The proof is entirely analytic and requires no computer-assisted verification.
item.dc:creator: Yutian Li

item.title: Lenses make many points: Pure point spectrum disproves Simon's $L^2$ conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.31637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $d\ge2$ and $0\le\sigma<1/3$, we construct with LLM-assistance a smooth bounded nonnegative lens-type potential $V$ with arbitrarily small $\|V\|_\infty+\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|x|^{1-d+\sigma}|V(x)|^2 dx$, such that $-\Delta+V$ has only pure point spectrum in $(0,\infty)$. Thus, we show that Barry Simon's $L^2$ conjecture, Problem 8 in "Schr\"odinger operators in the twenty-first century", is false.
item.dc:creator: Simon Becker, Mengxuan Yang

item.title: Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, II: local perturbations, the scattering matrix and an inverse problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.30575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Robin, or impedance, Laplacian on a half-space of dimension $n \ge 3$ which is perturbed inside a fixed ball. The boundary may be deformed, and obstacles may be present in the interior or attached to the boundary, in any combination and with no smallness assumption. Outside the ball the configuration is the flat impedance half-space of Part I, with constant impedance $\alpha > 0$, where a bulk channel and a surface channel propagate at every positive energy and only the surface channel propagates on the band $(-\alpha^2,0)$. We prove a limiting absorption principle, valid at every positive energy and outside a discrete set of embedded eigenvalues in the band. We construct the generalized Fourier transform and prove its completeness by a stationary argument which constructs no wave operator and reduces completeness to the uniqueness of the scattering solution at each energy. We then obtain the scattering matrix, its unitarity and a two-channel optical theorem. The main result is a uniqueness theorem for the inverse problem. Under two geometric conditions on the pair, the scattering amplitude at a single positive energy determines the perturbation completely, and the argument does not distinguish a deformation of the boundary from an obstacle. It follows that no nontrivial perturbation satisfying the same conditions is invisible at any positive energy. On the surface band the corresponding statement is reduced to one explicitly stated question about the exterior Robin problem.
item.dc:creator: Michiyuki Watanabe

item.title: A sharp gradient-corrected Lieb--Thirring inequality in one dimension with applications to density functional theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.30887v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We first prove a sharp Lieb-Thirring inequality with semi-classical constant and gradient correction in one dimension. In the periodic setting, the corresponding inequality also includes a parity dependent shell-correction term, which appears to be new. Moreover, we also characterize the optimizers of these inequalities. In particular, the optimizing density profiles form a two-dimensional manifold, which we call here the Poincar\'e density manifold. We then apply these results to study the Thomas--Fermi--von Weizs\"acker (TFW) approximation of the kinetic energy in Density Functional Theory. More precisely, we first obtain an explicit and non-asymptotic bound on the global and local error made by the TFW approximation. These bounds are controlled by the distance of the normalized density profile from the Poincar\'e density manifold times the number of particles. In particular, these bounds show that the TFW approximation is exact on the Poincar\'e manifold. We then show that, in the periodic setting, the distance between the Kohn-Sham potential and the inverse TFW potential in the natural dual Sobolev space can also be controlled by explicit density dependent constants times the distance to the Poincar\'e manifold. As a corollary, we prove that for a fixed density profile, the Kohn-Sham potential converges towards the inverse Thomas--Fermi potential in the high-density limit $N \rightarrow \infty$ with asymptotic rate of order $N^{-2}$. This rate is shown to be optimal.
item.dc:creator: Thiago Carvalho Corso, Louis Garrigue

item.title: A unified quantitative approach to Chiti and Kohler--Jobin inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.31063v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain two quantitative results related to classical rearrangement inequalities for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue. The first one is a quantitative version of Chiti's reverse H\"older inequality. More precisely, for every $1\le q<p<\infty$, we prove that the deficit controls, up to translations, the $L^q$ distance between a first eigenfunction of a bounded domain and the first eigenfunction of the ball having the same first eigenvalue. The second result concerns the Kohler--Jobin inequality and gives a quantitative estimate in terms of the $L^\infty\!\to L^2$ distance between the corresponding Dirichlet resolvents. In both cases, the main idea is to find a suitable superlevel set of the first eigenfunction which is almost optimal for the Faber-Krahn inequality.
item.dc:creator: Vincenzo Amato, Luca Barbato, Emanuele Cristoforoni, Alba Lia Masiello, Carlo Nitsch, Cristina Trombetti, Federico Villone
